sentences.text: This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 16-11-2023 at about 10.00 p.m., the petitioner after purchasing Tata Ace vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-13-C- 4789 was carrying another bike inside that vehicle, from Channarayapattna towards his village and the said vehicle was driven by its driver by name S.K. Raju, slowly and cautiously, on the correct side of the road, by observing all the traffic rules and regulations.

When they reached near Jayanthi Grama,
Kibbanahalli, Tiptur, at that time the driver of the car bearing Reg. No.KA-13-P-1894,
drove the same from K.B. Cross side with high speed, in rash and negligent manner,
endangering to human life and without observing the traffic rules and regulations Raghu .R. Alias Raghu vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39822083/
2 and without observing the movement of vehicles on the said road and dashed against the vehicle of the petitioner.

sentences.text: Due to the said impact, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Tiptur Government Hospital, wherein he took first aid treatment and then he was shifted to Hassan Government Hospital, wherein he took treatment as an in-patient.

Earlier to the accident, he was doing business of selling bangles, toys, domestic items and ladies cosmetic items at different open markets (santhes) in and around Tumkuru District and was also doing mason and coolie work and was earning a sum of Rs.40,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Kibbanahalli Police have registered the case against the driver of the said car, for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% per annum.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsel.
The respondent No.1 has filed its written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.2 did not choose to file his written statement.
4. The respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in favour of respondent No.2 in respect of car bearing Reg. No.KA-13-P- 1894 and it was valid as on the date of accident.
Further it has sought permission to seek protection under Section 147 and 149(2) of Motor Vehicles Act.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provisions under Section 134(C) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
Further, it has sought permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.2, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

Further it is contended that, as on the date of accident, the driver of the car was not holding valid and effective driving licence and the said vehicle was not having valid permit and fitness certificate.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries sustained, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.

Further it is contended that, as on the date of accident, the driver of the Tata Ace vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence and the said vehicle was not having valid permit and insurance policy.
The petitioner has not made owner of Tata Ace as one of the party to the petition.
Hence, the petition is liable to be dismissed for non joinder of necessary party.
Further it is contended that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tata Ace vehicle and dashing the same against the car.
The complaint has been lodged after lapse of 2 days from the date of accident.
Further it has contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

sentences.text: Issue No.1:

It is specific case of the petitioner that, on 16-11-2023 at about 10.00 p.m., when he was traveling in Tata Ace vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-13-C-4789, from Channarayapattna towards his village, the same being driven by its driver by name S.K. Raju, slowly and cautiously, on the correct side of the road, near Jayanthi Grama, Kibbanahalli, Tiptur, the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-13-P-1894, drove the same from K.B. Cross side with high speed, in rash and negligent manner, without observing the movement of vehicles on the said road and dashed against the vehicle of the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Tiptur Government Hospital,
wherein he took first aid treatment and then he was shifted to Hassan Government Hospital,
wherein he took treatment as an in- patient.

Earlier to the accident, he was doing business of selling bangles, toys, domestic items and ladies cosmetic items at different open markets (santhes) in and around Tumkuru District and was also doing mason and coolie work and was earning Rs.40,000/-
per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
10. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein he has reiterated entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of his oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked total 22 documents as Ex.P.1 to 22.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is true copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 is true copy of first information statement, Ex.P.3 is true copy of charge-sheet, Ex.P.4 is true copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P.5 is true copy of seizure mahazar, Ex.P.6 and 7 are Motor Vehicles Accident Reports (total 2), Ex.P.8 is true copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.9 is true copy of MLC register extract, Ex.P.10 is OPD slip, Ex.P.11 are medical bills (total 9), Ex.P.12 are prescriptions (total 7), Ex.P.13 is notarized copy of Aadhar card of petitioner, Ex.P.14 are OPD slips (total 4), Ex.P.15 are medical bills (total 4), Ex.P.16 is prescription, Ex.P.17 is discharge summary, Ex.P.18 are photos (total 3), Ex.P.19 is C.D., Ex.P.20 is certificate under Section 65B of Evidence Act, Ex.P.21 is OPD with calculation sheet and Ex.P.22 is x-ray.

11. On meticulously going through the above police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 9, prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-13-P-1894 in the turn of the road and dashing the same to oncoming Tata Ace vehicle of the petitioner.
Due to said impact the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries on his right leg and other parts of the body.

The investigation officer in his final report, marked as Ex.P.3, has clearly stated that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent driving of the offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-13-P-1894.
12.

At the outset, it is pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of car bearing Reg. No.KA-13-P-1894 in the said accident, issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.1 in respect of said vehicle and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

Further, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner has remained undisputed by the owner of offending vehicle/Respondent No.2, as he did not choose file his written statement and contest the case of the petitioner.

Whereas, the respondent No.1 insurance Raghu .R. Alias Raghu vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39822083/
5 company has specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and taken specific defence that, the said accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tata Ace vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-13-C-4789 himself, as he rode the same in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the car bearing Reg. No.KA-13-P-1894 and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the car bearing Reg. No.KA-13-P- 1894.

In order to establish the said contentions, the respondent No.1 has examined the Police Head Constable of Gubbi Police Station as R.W.1, who is the investigation officer who has conducted the investigation in respect of accident in question and foisted charge-sheet against the driver of car bearing Reg.
No.KA-13-P-1894.

He has clearly deposed in his evidence that, he has conducted the entire investigation in the case and found that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-13-P-1894 and hence, he has submitted the charge-sheet against the said driver.

Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.1, treating R.W.1 as hostile witness, has cross-examined in length, nothing worth has been brought out which goes to show that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Tata Ace vehicle or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-13-P-1894 in the turn of the road and dashing the same to Tata Ace vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-13-C-4789 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries on his right leg in the said accident.

Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which goes to show that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tata Ace vehicle or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.

13. Further, the Ex.P.4 spot mahazar also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on the left side of 30 feet wide on NH-73 road, near Jayanthi Grama, Kibbanahalli Hobli, Tipturu Taluk, Tumakuru District, in between the offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-13-P-1894 and the Tata Ace vehicle bearing No.KA-13-C-4789 of the petitioner.
Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Reports, which are marked as Ex.P.6 and 7, the accident has not taken place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the Tata Ace vehicle, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car.

Further, the investigation officer in his Ex.P.3 final report/charge-sheet has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-13-P-1894 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge- sheet has not been challenged either by the driver or the owner of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-13-P-1894.

In such circumstances,
there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, negligence of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

In such circumstances and for the reasons stated above, the ratio laid down in the above cited decisions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court and Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, relied by Raghu .R. Alias Raghu vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39822083/
6 the learned counsel for respondent No.1, are not applicable to the present facts and circumstances of the case.

sentences.text: 14. No doubt, there is a delay of 2 days in lodging the complaint by the petitioner.
But, the complainant has stated the reason for delay in lodging the complaint in his Ex.P.2 first information statement.
He has clearly stated that, as he was engaged in providing the treatment to the injured petitioner, there is delay caused in lodging the complaint.
It is settled proposition of law that, the delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt claimant's case in genuine cases.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Ravi V/s Badrinarayan and others, reported in (2011) 4 SCC 693, has clearly held that, "the delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt claimant's case in genuine cases.

entities.text: Ravi V/s Badrinarayan and others, reported in (2011) 4 SCC 693
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Indian conditions, it is not expected that a person would to rush to police station after accident.
The treatment of victim is given priority over lodging FIR.
The kith and kin of victim are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging FIR.
Hence, delay in lodging FIR not a ground to dismiss claim petition."

15. There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence on record by the respondents to disbelieve the reason for delay in lodging the complaint, stated in the Ex.P.1 First Information Report and Ex.P.2 first information statement.

In such circumstances and in the light of ratio laid down in the above cited decision, this Court is of the opinion that, in the present facts and circumstances of the case, the delay for lodging the complaint is properly explained by the petitioner with cogent and satisfactory reasons.

16. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.8 wound certificate, Ex.P.10 and 14 OPD slips (total 5), Ex.P.17 discharge summary, Ex.P.21 out-patient record with calculation sheet and Ex.P.22 x-ray, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident.
The petitioner has suffered fracture of lower one third of right femur.

The same is deposed by P.W.2,
who is the doctor who has clinically examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability.
On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence produced by the respondent No.1, to show that the above medical records are false documents.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can be safely held that, the respondent No.1 has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-13-P-1894 and injuries sustained to the petitioner in the said accident.
17. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011) 11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

19. Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 16-11-2023 at about 10:00 p.m., on NH-73 road, near Jayanthi Grama, Kibbanahalli Hobli, Tipturu Taluk, Tumakuru District,
due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-13-P-1894.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
20. Issue No.2:

While answering the above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-13-P-1894 and he has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
The medical records placed on record clearly speaks that, the petitioner has sustained fracture of lower one third of right femur and for the said injury he has undergone surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income:
In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of his Aadhar card, which is marked as Ex.P.13.
As per Ex.P.13, the date of birth of the petitioner is 24-02-2003.
The accident has taken place on 16-11-2023 at about 10:00 p.m.
Therefore, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 21 years.

Further, the P.W.2, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered fracture of lower one third of right femur.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that,
there is 33.24% physical disability of right lower limb and 16.62% physical disability to the whole body of the petitioner.

Further, the Ex.P.8 wound certificate, Ex.P.10 and 14 OPD slips (total 5), Ex.P.17 discharge summary, Ex.P.21 out-patient record with calculation sheet and Ex.P.22 x-ray clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered the above stated injury and he has undergone surgery for the said injury.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has cross-examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.

Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, there is no disability suffered by the petitioner as deposed in his evidence affidavit and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability.

But, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.2 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on Raghu .R. Alias Raghu vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39822083/
8 16-11-2023 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 20-03- 2025, which is after lapse of one year and seven months from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.

sentences.text: Further he has stated that, the petitioner requires one more surgery for removal of implants.
This clearly goes to show that, the disability has been assessed before the completion of full treatment to the petitioner.
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.

entities.text: Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: If the disability had been assessed after future surgery, perhaps there would have been reduction in the percentage of the disability.
Further it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.2 has considered half of the total disability to right lower limb and arrived at total disability to whole body at 16.62%.
Further, it is pertinent to note that, P.W.2 has clearly admitted in his cross- examination that, the fracture to the right femur is united with implants in situ.

Therefore, in such circumstances, taking into consideration the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence available on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 12% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.

Hence,
in the instant case the disability of 12% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.

a) The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was doing business of selling bangles, toys, domestic items and ladies cosmetic items at different open market (santhes) in and around Tumkuru District and was also doing mason and coolie work and was earning a sum of Rs.40,000/- per month.
Further, he has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do work or continue his avocation.
The respondent No.1 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.

He has not produced any document to show that, before accident he was doing business of selling bangles, toys, domestic items and ladies cosmetic items at different open market (santhes) in and around Tumkuru District and was also doing mason and coolie work and was earning a sum of Rs.40,000/- per month.
Therefore, in such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court, except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident took place in 2023.

Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.16,000/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,92,000/-.
b) As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 21 years is 18.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Therefore, loss of future income is Total annual income X disability/100 X multiplier = Rs.1,92,000 X 12/100 X 18 = Rs.4,14,720/-.
ii) Medical expenses:

The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.6,00,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc.
In order to prove the same, he has produced 13 medical bills, as per Ex.P.11 and 15.
All the bills have been examined carefully and found that the petitioner has spend total amount of Rs.6,320/- towards medical expenses.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.6,320/- under the head of medical expenses.

sentences.text: In the present case, the petitioner has sustained grievous injury i.e. fracture of lower one third of right femur.
As per Ex.P.17 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 7 days from 17-11-2023 to 23-11-2023, in Sri Chamarajendra HIMS Teaching Hospital, Hassan.
Further, as per P.W.2, the said injuries have caused physical disability to the petitioner.
In such circumstances, certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.

Therefore, taking into considering the injuries sustained and disability to the petitioner,
this Court is of the opinion that, an compensation amount of Rs.50,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.
iv) Attendant charges:
As per Ex.P.17 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 7 days in Sri Chamarajendra HIMS Teaching Hospital, Hassan.
He might have spent considerable amount towards attendant charges during that period.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.1000 x 7 = Rs.7,000/- is awarded towards the attendant charges.
v) Food and nourishment:
As per Ex.P.17 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 7 days in Sri Chamarajendra HIMS Teaching Hospital, Hassan.
He might have spent considerable amount towards food and nourishment during that period.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.800 x 7 = Rs.5,600/- is awarded towards food and nourishment charges.
vi) Conveyance expenses:

The petitioner is the resident of Thimmalipalya, Adalagere Post, Nitturu Hobli, Gubbi Taluk, Tumkuru District, the accident has taken place on NH-73 road, near Jayanthi Grama, Kibbanahalli Hobli, Tipturu Taluk, Tumakuru District and the petitioner has taken treatment at Sri Chamarajendra HIMS Teaching Hospital, Hassan.
Taking into consideration the distance in between the above places, compensation of Rs.10,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.
vii) Loss of income during treatment period:
The petitioner has taken treatment for 7 days as in-patient at Sri Chamarajendra HIMS Teaching Hospital, Hassan, for the grievous injuries sustained by him.
He might have taken rest for about 2 months and lost his income for the said period.
Therefore, Rs.16,000 x 2 = Rs.32,000/- is awarded towards loss of income during treatment period.
viii) Loss of amenities:
It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 21 years and unfortunately he has suffered fracture of lower one third of right femur.
Further, he has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 12% to the whole body.
Therefore, awarding compensation of Rs.30,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.
ix) Future medical expenses:
The P.W.2 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner needs to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants.
But, admittedly the P.W.2 has not issued estimation of cost for the said surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards future medical expenses would be just and reasonable.

21. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows:

22. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-13-P- 1894.
The insurance policy bearing No.990000312303168837, issued by the respondent No.1, in respect of offending car bearing No.KA-13-P-1894 was valid from 06-06-2023 to 05-06-2024.
As such, the said policy was valid as on the date of accident i.e. 16-11-2023.
There is no evidence on record to show that, there is any breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy issued by the respondent No.1.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that,
due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-13-P-1894 the accident in question has taken place.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.2 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.1 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.2.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.1 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the Tata Ace vehicle, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car.
Further, the investigation officer in his Ex.P.3 final report/charge-sheet has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-13-P-1894 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge- sheet has not been challenged either by the driver or the owner of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-13-P-1894.
In such circumstances,
there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, negligence of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
14. No doubt, there is a delay of 2 days in lodging the complaint by the petitioner.
But, the complainant has stated the reason for delay in lodging the complaint in his Ex.P.2 first information statement.
He has clearly stated that, as he was engaged in providing the treatment to the injured petitioner, there is delay caused in lodging the complaint.
It is settled proposition of law that, the delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt claimant's case in genuine cases.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Ravi V/s Badrinarayan and others, reported in (2011) 4 SCC 693, has clearly held that, "the delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt claimant's case in genuine cases.
The treatment of victim is given priority over lodging FIR.
In such circumstances and in the light of ratio laid down in the above cited decision, this Court is of the opinion that, in the present facts and circumstances of the case, the delay for lodging the complaint is properly explained by the petitioner with cogent and satisfactory reasons.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can be safely held that, the respondent No.1 has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-13-P-1894 and injuries sustained to the petitioner in the said accident.
17. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011) 11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."
18. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, " in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone Raghu .R. This clearly goes to show that, the disability has been assessed before the completion of full treatment to the petitioner.
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.
If the disability had been assessed after future surgery, perhaps there would have been reduction in the percentage of the disability.
Therefore, in such circumstances, taking into consideration the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence available on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 12% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.

in the instant case the disability of 12% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
He has not produced any document to show that, before accident he was doing business of selling bangles, toys, domestic items and ladies cosmetic items at different open market (santhes) in and around Tumkuru District and was also doing mason and coolie work and was earning a sum of Rs.40,000/- per month.
